top_choice_rationale: P003 (Katori and Ye) rewards a specific, reproduced principle: magic-wavelength trapping cancels the lattice light shift so many neutral atoms can be interrogated in parallel, a step distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. Independent laboratories agree at the 10^-18 level, the attribution is the cleanest on the slate (a proposer and the leading realiser, with the citation resting on the invention and not on stability alone), and the redefinition of the second is a metrology schedule matter, not a test of the physics. I rank P001 next because its Z2 and HgTe observation are mature and distinct from 2016, but the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang is a real gap in the prediction chain. P002 follows because the flat-band prediction and correlated phases are real and replicated, while twist-angle disorder and concentrated experimental credit make it less settled this year. An award is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: Possible but not disqualifying: a research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, where Hall is a close scientific neighbour of Jun Ye (P003), and my own atomic-physics and precision-laser-spectroscopy background; no documented direct collaboration with Katori or Ye, and none with the other credited names.
